newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy ends up on Brazil fire, overdone ideas.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy ends up on Brazil fire, overdone ideas.

text.p: Ideas that a small fire at the key Brazilian port of Paranagua would slow that country's exports pushed CBOT soybean futures to a sharply higher close Tuesday, traders said.
"There's been some concern that exports out of Brazil will be slowed by the fire," said one CBOT floor trader.
The fire, which put one of five grain loading conveyor belts at the port out of service for five to ten days, was seen having little impact on exports, Brazil traders said.
Ideas that Monday's losses were overdone also contributed to Tuesday's strength, CBOT traders and analysts said.
"I think this rally was more about value than the fire," said Mickey Luth, analyst with the Laifa Group in Chicago.
"Monday's losses were overdone, particularly going into a report that could be bullish," Luth said.
On Monday, the U.S. Department of Agriculture will release soybean acreage estimates based on farmer surveys. Early trade estimates have ranged from 65.50 million to 66.47 million acres.
CBOT soybeans settled up 1-1/2 to 10-1/4 cents per bushel, with May soybeans up 10-1/4 at $8.42 a bushel. July settled up 11 cents at $8.43-3/4.
Concerns that the soil in Argentina is too dry also helped buoy prices, floor traders said.

Overly dry weather in recent weeks was seen reducing soybean production, and many private estimates were slipping near 12.5 million tonnes from previous forecasts that were closer to 13 million, traders said.
On the day, Refco traded 2.5 million bushels of May, Smith Barney bought one million July and three million May, and R.J. O'Brien bought 1.5 million May and two million July, traders said.

In options trade, ADM bought 500 July $8.50 calls and sold 500 July $8.75 calls, floor sources said. Rosenthal Collins bought 400 November $7.50 calls and Tradelink bought 500 May $7.50 puts and sold 500 May $8.25 puts.
Volume was estimated by the CBOT at 50,000 contracts, compared with Monday's actual volume of 42,485 contracts.
